name: Ikaranggal
world_status: a description exists but is not accessible

earlier_scan.note: Extinct Australian; Glottolog lists only Sommer subclassification notes, no description

new_statements.citation: Sutton, Peter J. 1976. The diversity of initial dropping languages in southern Cape York. In Peter Sutton (ed.), Languages of Cape York, 102-123. Canberra: Australian Institute of Aboriginal Studies
new_statements.check: reported on verification, not yet confirmed
new_statements.second_reader_evidence: Only one work is listed and it was partially opened, so no silent/not-opened works exist to spot-check; instead I re-searched the same volume with 61 further full-text queries (saved). Nothing new about Ikaranggal stress: the scanned variant 'Ikavanggal' (missed by the compiler) adds two mentions, both about dialect identity ('a quantity of another dialect, Ikavanggal.. The data suggest that Ikavanggal is a more distant dialect, although probably its speakers comprised part of the loose Koko-Mini confederation'), at scanned page marker 134 in Sommer's 'Roth's Peninsular Vocabularies', not Sutton's chapter. The exceptions to Sutton's group-level principle are now retrieved (Ogho-Ndjan, Oykan…

sources.citation: Sommer, Bruce A. 1969. Kunjen phonology: synchronic and diachronic. Pacific Linguistics B-11. Canberra: ANU
sources.note: Stress rules (pp. 29-31) are for Oykangand and said to hold for Olgol, Okunjan, Kawarrangg; its 'Koko-Mini' is grouped with Kawarrangg-Okunjan (subgroup B, p. 15) and is not the Thaypanic Ikarranggal of Sommer 1999. Not applicable to ikar1243.

sources.citation: Glottolog 5.3 languoid ikar1243 and its reference list (8 refs: Sommer n.d; Palmer 1884 JRAI; Palmer 1886 in Curr; Ray 1907; Sommer 1976 Roth's Peninsular Vocabularies; AUSTLANG; Ethnologue 2016; ISO CR 2012-138); github md.ini for ikar1243, cent2337, alay1234
sources.note: Bibliographic only. Only descriptive item is Sommer n.d. (grammar sketch, 34 pp.); classification per Alpher 'Thaypanic' (Central Alaya-Athima); altnames include Akoonkoon, Gugu/Kuku Mini, Roth's Koko-Mini.

sources.citation: AUSTLANG Y198 'Ogh Ikarranggal' (AIATSIS collection.aiatsis.gov.au/austlang/language/y198), Internet Archive copy 2024
sources.note: Nothing on stress. Documentation table lists word list / grammar / text collection / audio-visual all 'None'; references Alpher 2016 (location per 'Sommer in Alpher 2016:42'), Oates 1975, Dixon 2002, Rigsby 2005, Sommer 1999 (PMS 5918).

sources.citation: Round, Erich R. / Bowern, Claire — CHIRILA-AusPhon metadata ( in JaydenM-C/PN_treebuilding, 2020) and Round's PHOIBLE inventory bibliography (bambooforest/phoible-scripts)
sources.note: Nothing on stress. Records that the Ikarranggal lexicon and inventory come from sommer_ikarranggal_1999 (= Glottolog 320043, 'published', Ethnografix) with a grammar-harvester file ''; Gugu Mini / Kookobatha / Okuntjel wordlists mapped to ikar1243 per Alpher 2016:42.

sources.citation: ISO 639-3 Registration Authority. 2012. Change Request 2012-138 (split [ggr] into [gtu], [ggm], [ikr]) and the new-code form Aristar, supported by Bowern)
sources.note: Nothing on stress. Classification Rarmul Pama (Oates 1975:287, 292); no published sources listed on the ikr form.

sources.citation: PHOIBLE 2.0 inventories ER 2878 Ikarranggal (source Sommer 1999) and ER 2879 Takalak (source Sutton 1976), contributed by Erich Round

sources.citation: Oates, Lynette F. 1975. The 1973 supplement to a revised linguistic survey of Australia. Armidale: Armidale Christian Book Centre, p. 292 (entry 118.3c Ikarranggal; one-page AUSTLANG extract)
sources.note: Nothing on stress. Survey entry: 'Known as Koko-Crayfish (BAS)'; notes a vowel 'reflection rule' (initial-dropping) and that 'Sommer recorded a long word list, brief grammar and texts from an informant at Cannibal Creek, who has since died.'

sources.citation: Sommer, Bruce A. 1999. Ikarranggal. Townsville, QLD: Ethnografix, 34 pp. (= AIATSIS manuscript PMS 5918; Glottolog ref 320043 'Sommer n.d. Ikarranggal. Ms. 34pp.', listed by Glottolog as a grammar sketch)
sources.tag: likely states stress; not yet obtained
sources.access_detail: print only (no digital copy found when the work was looked up)
sources.note: The only grammatical description of the language; PHOIBLE (Round) took a 23-segment inventory from it and Oates reports Sommer recorded 'a long word list, brief grammar and texts'; a 34-page sketch by Sommer (who gave explicit stress rules in his 1969 Kunjen phonology) is the one place a first-hand stress statement would exist.

sources.note: Comparative-historical treatment of the Alaya-Athima/Thaypanic group using Sommer's Ikarranggal data (AUSTLANG cites 'Sommer in Alpher 2016:42'); initial-dropping discussions in this area routinely invoke stress placement, so it may state or imply the Ikarranggal pattern second-hand.

sources.citation: Sommer, Bruce A. 1972-1999. Ikarranggal materials in the Bruce A. Sommer Papers, UQFL476, Fryer Library, University of Queensland (collection dates 1964-2003; finding aid last updated 22/11/2022): Box 30 Item 11 'Ikarranggal' = (a) 'Ikarranggal pp34 comb bound description by Bruce Sommer 4/99' [a copy of Sommer 1999 Ikarranggal, AIATSIS PMS 5918 = known rows 9/14/16], (b) 'Ikarranggal analysis notes with computer printout of lexical analysis [various dates]. Ikarranggal 19/7/72', (c) 'Ikarranggal from West field tape 1447-8, 9/7/73 (with some Anggula)'; Box 31 field tapes 73-9 (Chillagoe, Ikaranggal, Caesar Lee Chen (Choo), 10 Jul 1973), 73-10 (Ikarankal) and C74-24 (Aloomba, Ikaranggal, Willie Lee Chen (Choo), 10 Apr 1974; cassette dub in Box 5); Box 5 cassettes 7-9 (Michael Walsh, Ikarranggal, 1973?).
sources.tag: likely states tone; not yet obtained
sources.note: The deposit holds a library copy of Sommer's 34-pp 1999 Ikarranggal description (the only phonological/grammatical description of the language, otherwise unlocated) together with his unpublished 1972 lexical-analysis notes, a 1973 transcription from La Mont West's field tape 1447-8 and the 1973-74 field audio; contents unseen; for a Thaypanic (Pama-Nyungan) language the expected prosodic statement is stress placement and no lexical tone, which only the description component could supply.

tone.says: The deposit holds a library copy of Sommer's 34-pp 1999 Ikarranggal description (the only phonological/grammatical description of the language, otherwise unlocated) together with his unpublished 1972 lexical-analysis notes, a 1973 transcription from La Mont West's field tape 1447-8 and the 1973-74 field audio; contents unseen; for a Thaypanic (Pama-Nyungan) language the expected prosodic statement is stress placement and no lexical tone, which only the description component could supply.
